candidates.name: Islamic Arts Museum

candidates.name: Malay World Ethnology Museum

candidates.name: Galeria Sri Perdana
candidates.content: The building, where this museum is housed, was the official residence of Tun Dr. Mahathir Mohamad, the fourth Prime Minister of Malaysia. Artefacts and personal collection of Dr. Mahathir are exhibited here.

candidates.name: Muzium Telekom
candidates.price: RM11 for foreign adults and RM5 for children
candidates.content: Built in 1928 as the Central Battery Telephone Exchange, converted into the Telecommunications Museum in 1994, showing the growth of communications technology in Malaysia. A rather limited amount of antique telecom equipment on di

candidates.name: Muzium Orang Asli

candidates.name: National Planetarium
candidates.price: Gallery: free; Planetarium show: adult RM12, child RM8
candidates.content: The attractions here include space science and astronomy exhibits, a theatre screening 3-Dimensional movies, a viewing gallery and an observatory.

candidates.name: Royal Malaysian Police Museum
candidates.content: The police museum shows the history of the Malaysian police with pictures, weapons and vehicles.

candidates.name: Muzium Diraja
candidates.content: The former palace of the electoral king of Malaysia, complete with all the royal splendor one might expect.

candidates.name: Istana Budaya

candidates.name: Independence Square

candidates.name: Kuala Lumpur Railway Station

candidates.name: National Palace
candidates.content: The official residence of the King (Yang Di-Pertuan Agong) of Malaysia. You can get a glance at this gigantic building by going to the main entrance (see geo marker). If the flag is raised up on top of the largest dome of the pala

candidates.name: National Science Centre
candidates.content: Well done science museum, which is especially great, if you come with children.

candidates.name: Orchid Garden
candidates.content: The Orchid garden was opened in 1986. 700-800 species of orchids can be seen here. Malaysia has 3000 species altogether. There is a souvenir shop on the premises.

candidates.name: Bird Park
candidates.price: Adult RM67, child RM45 for foreigners

candidates.name: Butterfly Park
candidates.price: RM22 (children RM10) plus another RM4 if you wish to use your video camera
candidates.content: Walk-through tropical butterfly enclosure. Apparently the largest butterfly garden in the world spanning over 80,000 sq ft of landscaped garden with over 5,000 live butterflies, exotic plants, butterfly-host plants and ferns.

candidates.name: Petronas Twin Towers

candidates.price: Foreigners/Malaysians: adults RM50/38, children RM40/28, Seniors RM30/28
candidates.content: A gigantic aquarium housing over 5,000 aquatic and terrestrial species. The aquarium has many displays including an underwater tunnel, interactive touch pools, exhibits of flora and fauna and multimedia kiosks. They also have feed

candidates.content: Guided tours through the rainforest. Includes a canopy walk and a little museum. In 2025 the institute and forest was listed as a .

candidates.name: ASEAN Sculpture Garden
candidates.content: A sculpture garden, located next to National Monument in walking distance.

candidates.name: National Mosque

candidates.name: KLCC Park

candidates.name: Petronas Philharmonic Hall

candidates.name: Badminton
candidates.content: Built in 1990, the stadium can hold 4,500 spectators.

candidates.name: Berjaya Times Square Theme Park
candidates.price: Foreigners/Malaysians: adults RM48/38, children RM38/28, family (2 adults & 2 children) RM138/106

candidates.price: Foreigners: adult RM40, child (6-16) RM 5; Malaysians: RM10/1

candidates.name: Hike in Taman Tugu
candidates.content: Some beautiful rain forest pathways.

candidates.name: Watch an event at Bukit Jalil National Stadium
candidates.content: This huge stadium with a capacity of 87,411 is used as venue for many sports events and concerts.

candidates.content: The most popular spot in the whole city to go mountainbiking or hiking. Unfortunately the forest is constantly reduced in size by greedy building developers.

candidates.name: Pamper Zone

candidates.content: Olympic size pool. The opening hours are a little weird though: 7 one-hourly sessions on weekdays and 3 evening sessions on the weekends.

candidates.content: Restaurant, which houses live performances - mainly jazz - on almost every weekend. Local and international artists are performing.

candidates.name: The Social
candidates.content: Popular bar and restaurant.Can get quite noisy due to the large crowd.

candidates.name: Reggae Bar
candidates.content: It is a hostel bar so it is popular with backpackers. They also serve Asian and Western food. Also a hostel!

candidates.name: Heli Lounge
candidates.content: Amazing location on a helipad high above the city with amazing views.

candidates.name: San Francisco Coffee Express
candidates.content: Hot and cold coffee beverages and delicious cakes of all kinds.

candidates.name: Nasi Kandar Pelita

candidates.name: Annalakshmi Vegetarian Restaurant
candidates.price: From RM 10 for lunch or dinner

candidates.name: Chat Masala
candidates.content: This vegetarian restaurant serves mock meat. Go for the "mutton" or "chicken" briyani, tea-time specials like pani puri or bhel puri, then wash it down with filter coffee.

candidates.name: Dharma Realm Monastery Canteen
candidates.content: Great vegetarian food prepared by volunteers. Earnings are used to maintain the temple. A favourite among local office workers. The food is free of charge on Fridays and Sundays. Feel free to leave a donation though.

candidates.name: Havana Bar and Grill

candidates.content: Check out the food court on Level 2 of Plaza City One for its Indian, Pakistani and Bangladeshi cuisine. Recommended: Hanif Mughal Food (stall 5), Nasi Arab (stall 3) and Punjabi Vegetarian Food (stall 8).

candidates.name: Soong Kee Beef Noodles
candidates.content: This is a well-known KL beef noodle shop, it is said to have started operating since 1945. It serves the noodles "dry" with beef mince while the beef balls are given separately in a bowl of soup.

candidates.name: Sin Kiew Yee Shin Kee Beef Noodles
candidates.content: Also very traditional beef noodles like before, but more choices and also very popular with locals and tourists. 3 different noodles, 3 different ways of beef, dry or wet.

candidates.name: Jaya Restoran
candidates.price: RM8-14 for an average lunch w/o drinks
candidates.content: Great selection of Indian dishes. Very fresh ingredients. Especially the lunch buffet is highly recommended.

candidates.name: Kaveri
candidates.price: RM1 for roti canai, RM4-5 for meat
candidates.content: Open fronted restaurant with friendly staff. Serves a variety of Indian foods, plenty of meat dishes, as well as a number of vegetarian options.

candidates.name: Megamall & The Gardens

candidates.name: Berjaya Times Square
